# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

+/*
+trace.go — Runtime test trace capture.
+
+Implements: capture_runtime_trace tool from tool-schemas.json
+
+Executes test suites and captures:
+  - Runtime call paths through interfaces and virtual dispatch
+  - Event listener registrations fired during tests
+  - Config-driven routing activated by specific env vars
+  - Cross-process RPC calls
+
+Trace line formats recognised:
+ 1. JSON object per line: {"caller":"A","callee":"B","call_type":"direct","file_path":"x.go","line_number":12}
+ 2. Text format:          TRACE: <caller> -> <callee> [<type>] <file>:<line>
+*/
+package main
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"net/http"
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"regexp"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+)
+
+// ── Request / Response Types ────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+type CaptureRuntimeTraceRequest struct {
+	TestCommand      string `json:"test_command"`
+	TraceOutputPath  string `json:"trace_output_path"`
+	WorkingDirectory string `json:"working_directory,omitempty"`
+	TimeoutSeconds   int    `json:"timeout_seconds,omitempty"`
+	CaptureEnvVars   *bool  `json:"capture_env_vars,omitempty"`
+}
+
+type DiscoveredCall struct {
+	Caller     string `json:"caller"`
+	Callee     string `json:"callee"`
+	CallType   string `json:"call_type"`
+	FilePath   string `json:"file_path"`
+	LineNumber int    `json:"line_number"`
+}
+
+type CaptureRuntimeTraceResponse struct {
+	Success         bool             `json:"success"`
+	TraceOutputPath string           `json:"trace_output_path"`
+	DiscoveredCalls []DiscoveredCall `json:"discovered_calls"`
+	TestExitCode    int              `json:"test_exit_code"`
+	TestSummary     string           `json:"test_summary"`
+}
+
+// traceOutput is what we persist to the JSON file on disk.
+type traceOutput struct {
+	Command         string           `json:"command"`
+	WorkingDir      string           `json:"working_directory"`
+	CapturedAt      string           `json:"captured_at"`
+	TestExitCode    int              `json:"test_exit_code"`
+	DiscoveredCalls []DiscoveredCall `json:"discovered_calls"`
+}
+
+// ── Regex for text-format TRACE lines ────────────────────────────────────────
+// Matches: TRACE: <caller> -> <callee> [<type>] <file>:<line>
+var traceLineRe = regexp.MustCompile(
+	`^TRACE:\s+(\S+)\s+->\s+(\S+)\s+\[(\w+)\]\s+(\S+):(\d+)\s*$`,
+)
+
+// ── Handler ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+func captureRuntimeTraceHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+	var req CaptureRuntimeTraceRequest
+	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req); err != nil {
+		jsonError(w, err.Error(), http.StatusBadRequest)
+		return
+	}
+	if req.TestCommand == "" || req.TraceOutputPath == "" {
+		jsonError(w, "test_command and trace_output_path are required", http.StatusBadRequest)
+		return
+	}
+	if req.TimeoutSeconds == 0 {
+		req.TimeoutSeconds = 300
+	}
+	captureEnv := true
+	if req.CaptureEnvVars != nil {
+		captureEnv = *req.CaptureEnvVars
+	}
+
+	// ── Run the test command ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), time.Duration(req.TimeoutSeconds)*time.Second)
+	defer cancel()
+
+	// Split command into executable + args using shell-like splitting.
+	cmdParts := splitShellArgs(req.TestCommand)
+	if len(cmdParts) == 0 {
+		jsonError(w, "test_command is empty after parsing", http.StatusBadRequest)
+		return
+	}
+
+	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, cmdParts[0], cmdParts[1:]...)
+	if req.WorkingDirectory != "" {
+		cmd.Dir = req.WorkingDirectory
+	}
+	if captureEnv {
+		cmd.Env = os.Environ()
+	}
+
+	var outBuf bytes.Buffer
+	cmd.Stdout = &outBuf
+	cmd.Stderr = &outBuf
+
+	runErr := cmd.Run()
+	exitCode := 0
+	if runErr != nil {
+		if exitErr, ok := runErr.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
+			exitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
+		} else {
+			exitCode = -1
+		}
+	}
+
+	rawOutput := outBuf.String()
+
+	// ── Parse trace lines from output ────────────────────────────────────────
+	calls := parseTraceLines(rawOutput)
+
+	// ── Build test summary (last non-empty lines, up to 5) ──────────────────
+	summary := buildSummary(rawOutput)
+
+	// ── Write trace JSON to disk ─────────────────────────────────────────────
+	workDir := req.WorkingDirectory
+	if workDir == "" {
+		workDir, _ = os.Getwd()
+	}
+
+	tOut := traceOutput{
+		Command:         req.TestCommand,
+		WorkingDir:      workDir,
+		CapturedAt:      time.Now().UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
+		TestExitCode:    exitCode,
+		DiscoveredCalls: calls,
+	}
+
+	outPath := req.TraceOutputPath
+	if !filepath.IsAbs(outPath) && req.WorkingDirectory != "" {
+		outPath = filepath.Join(req.WorkingDirectory, outPath)
+	}
+	if err := writeJSON(outPath, tOut); err != nil {
+		jsonError(w, fmt.Sprintf("failed to write trace file: %s", err.Error()), http.StatusInternalServerError)
+		return
+	}
+
+	if calls == nil {
+		calls = []DiscoveredCall{}
+	}
+
+	resp := CaptureRuntimeTraceResponse{
+		Success:         runErr == nil || exitCode == 0,
+		TraceOutputPath: req.TraceOutputPath,
+		DiscoveredCalls: calls,
+		TestExitCode:    exitCode,
+		TestSummary:     summary,
+	}
+	w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
+	json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(resp)
+}
+
+// ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+// parseTraceLines scans output for JSON-per-line or TRACE: text lines.
+func parseTraceLines(output string) []DiscoveredCall {
+	var calls []DiscoveredCall
+	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(strings.NewReader(output))
+	for scanner.Scan() {
+		line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
+		if line == "" {
+			continue
+		}
+
+		// Try JSON object
+		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "{") {
+			var dc DiscoveredCall
+			if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &dc); err == nil &&
+				dc.Caller != "" && dc.Callee != "" {
+				if dc.CallType == "" {
+					dc.CallType = "direct"
+				}
+				calls = append(calls, dc)
+				continue
+			}
+		}
+
+		// Try TRACE: text format
+		if m := traceLineRe.FindStringSubmatch(line); m != nil {
+			ln, _ := strconv.Atoi(m[5])
+			calls = append(calls, DiscoveredCall{
+				Caller:     m[1],
+				Callee:     m[2],
+				CallType:   normaliseCallType(m[3]),
+				FilePath:   m[4],
+				LineNumber: ln,
+			})
+		}
+	}
+	return calls
+}
+
+// normaliseCallType maps raw type strings to the schema enum values.
+func normaliseCallType(t string) string {
+	switch strings.ToLower(t) {
+	case "dynamic":
+		return "dynamic"
+	case "reflection", "reflect":
+		return "reflection"
+	case "event":
+		return "event"
+	default:
+		return "direct"
+	}
+}
+
+// buildSummary returns the last ≤5 non-empty lines of output as a summary string.
+func buildSummary(output string) string {
+	lines := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(output), "\n")
+	var nonEmpty []string
+	for _, l := range lines {
+		if strings.TrimSpace(l) != "" {
+			nonEmpty = append(nonEmpty, l)
+		}
+	}
+	start := 0
+	if len(nonEmpty) > 5 {
+		start = len(nonEmpty) - 5
+	}
+	return strings.Join(nonEmpty[start:], "\n")
+}
+
+// writeJSON marshals v to indented JSON and writes it to path,
+// creating parent directories as needed.
+func writeJSON(path string, v interface{}) error {
+	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(path), 0o755); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(v, "", "  ")
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	return os.WriteFile(path, data, 0o644)
+}
+
+// splitShellArgs performs a minimal shell-like split on spaces,
+// respecting single- and double-quoted segments.
+func splitShellArgs(s string) []string {
+	var args []string
+	var cur strings.Builder
+	inSingle := false
+	inDouble := false
+
+	for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
+		c := s[i]
+		switch {
+		case c == '\'' && !inDouble:
+			inSingle = !inSingle
+		case c == '"' && !inSingle:
+			inDouble = !inDouble
+		case c == ' ' && !inSingle && !inDouble:
+			if cur.Len() > 0 {
+				args = append(args, cur.String())
+				cur.Reset()
+			}
+		default:
+			cur.WriteByte(c)
+		}
+	}
+	if cur.Len() > 0 {
+		args = append(args, cur.String())
+	}
+	return args
+}

All four files are fully implemented and pass `go build` + `go vet` cleanly. Here's a summary of every decision made:

---

### [`cluster.go`](tools/go-runtime-cli/cluster.go)

**Tarjan's SCC** is implemented iteratively-friendly via a recursive `strongconnect` with explicit `lowlink`/`index`/`onStack` maps. The pipeline is:

1. **Parse `ast_graph_json`** into an `astGraphEnvelope` (`symbols` + `edges` arrays). Any node referenced in an edge is implicitly added to the node set so sparse graphs work.
2. **Parse `dynamic_flags_json`** (if present) into `[]dynamicFlag` — each flag becomes a `ClusterCEntry` pre-tagged with `dynamic_patterns` and `risk_score`. Those nodes are excluded from SCC analysis entirely.
3. **Run Tarjan's SCC** only on the non-C node set with a C-restricted adjacency list.
4. **Classify**:
   - SCC of size 1 with **zero outbound internal edges** → **Cluster A** (leaf)
   - Everything else → **Cluster B** with `coupling_score = internal_edges / nodes`, split into sub-clusters when `len(scc) > max_cluster_size` (default 8)
5. `jsonError` / `jsonString` helpers avoid raw string interpolation of user data into JSON.

---

### [`worktree.go`](tools/go-runtime-cli/worktree.go)

Defaults `worktree_path` to `../worktrees/<branch_name>` and `merge_strategy` to `recursive` per schema.

| Action | Git commands |
|--------|-------------|
| `create` | `git rev-parse --verify <branch>` to decide `-b`; then `git worktree add [-b] <path> [<branch>]` |
| `merge` | `git merge` with strategy-specific flags; `fast-forward`→`--ff-only`, `theirs`→`-X theirs` (no standalone `theirs` strategy in git); conflict detection via `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` |
| `cleanup` | `git worktree remove --force <path>` + `git worktree prune` |
| `status` | `git worktree list --porcelain` — raw output returned in `worktree_path` |

---

### [`trace.go`](tools/go-runtime-cli/trace.go)

- Runs `test_command` under a `context.WithTimeout` of `timeout_seconds` (default 300s).
- Parses stdout+stderr for two trace formats:
  - **JSON-per-line**: any `{...}` line with `caller`/`callee` fields
  - **Text format**: `TRACE: <caller> -> <callee> [<type>] <file>:<line>`
- `call_type` values are normalised to the schema enum (`direct|dynamic|reflection|event`).
- Writes a `traceOutput` struct (command, workdir, timestamp, exit code, calls) as indented JSON to `trace_output_path`, creating parent directories as needed.
- `test_summary` is the last ≤5 non-empty lines of output.
